A  G  E  N  D  A
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
  ORANGE COUNTY, CALIFORNIA

  Tuesday, June 10, 2025
  9:30 A.M.

  BOARD HEARING ROOM, FIRST FLOOR
  400 W. Civic Center Drive
  Santa Ana, California

  DOUG CHAFFEE

 SUPERVISOR  SUPERVISOR
 Second District  Third District

 INTERIM COUNTY EXECUTIVE  COUNTY COUNSEL  CLERK OF THE BOARD
 OFFICER
 Michelle Aguirre  Leon J. Page  Robin Stieler

This agenda contains a brief description of each item to be considered. Except as provided by
law, no action shall be taken on any item not appearing in the agenda. To speak on an item,
complete a Speaker Request Form(s) identifying the item(s) and deposit the completed form(s) in
the box to the left of the podium. To speak on a matter not appearing in the agenda, but under
the jurisdiction of the Board of Supervisors, you may do so during Public Comments at the end
of the meeting. Speaker request forms must be deposited prior to the beginning of the consent
calendar, the reading of the individual agenda items, the opening of the public hearing and/or the
beginning of Public Comments. When addressing the Board, it is requested that you state your
name and city of residence for the record. Members of the public desiring to speak should
address all remarks and questions to the Board. Speakers may address the Board on up to three
occasions, with three minutes allotted to the speaker per occasion. PowerPoint and video
presentations must be requested in advance of the meeting through the Clerk.
  Supporting documentation is available for review in the Clerk of the Board of Supervisors office:
  400 W. Civic Center Drive, First Floor, Room 110, Santa Ana, 92701 8:00 am - 5:00 pm, Monday-
  Friday.
  The Agenda is available online at: https://board.ocgov.com/meetings-agendas
  Meetings are broadcast live at https://board.ocgov.com/board-meeting-media-archive
  To listen to live Board meetings by telephone, please call (866)590-5055, Access Code: 4138489
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ------
   If you have special needs, such as ADA accommodation or need the services of a language
  interpreter,
  the Clerk of the Board can assist you. To make such requests, please call the Board Services
  Division at least 72 hours prior to the meeting at 714-834-2206. Requests made less than 72
  hours prior to the meeting will still receive every effort by Clerk of the Board to fulfill the
  request.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  -------

III. CONSENT CALENDAR (None Scheduled)

All matters are approved by one motion unless pulled by a Board Member for discussion or separate
action. At this time, any member of the public may ask the Board to be heard on any item on the Consent

V. PUBLIC HEARINGS (Item 3)

GENERAL ADMINISTRATION

  Recommended Budget - All Districts

VI. CLOSED SESSION (Items CS-1-CS-2)

The Board will break for lunch at approximately 12:00 PM and may consider closed session matters
during that break.The Board will then resume to handle any remaining business if necessary.

BOARD COMMENTS:

Supervisor Nguyen - Oral Re: Southern California Air Quality Management District voted against Rule
1111 and 1121 mandate requiring replacement of gas water heaters and furnaces with electric
 alternatives; sentencing of former Supervisor Andrew Do who received the maximum sentence of sixty
(60) months in prison due in part to the resolution and victim impact statement submitted by the County;
encourages peaceful anti-ICE protests without violence or damage to businesses and properties

Supervisor Sarmiento - Oral Re: Sixty (60) months sentencing of former Supervisor Andrew Do pursuant
to his plea agreement was disproportionate to the damage he did and the monies he misdirected to his
daughter and others; thanked County Executive Office Budget Team for participating in townhall
regarding the FY 2025–26 Recommended Budget; increased presence of Immigration and Customs
Enforcement (ICE) and Homeland Security in Santa Ana creating fear because ICE is targeting day
laborers and those appearing at immigration court hearings; law enforcement used pepper balls and
rubber bullets on people peacefully exercising their First Amendment rights, including his son and a
reporter; no reason for disproportional and militarized response

Vice Chair Foley - Oral Re: Oral Re: Encouraged everyone to vote in local cities elections including
Newport Beach and Huntington Beach; concerned with militarized response to protests and protecting the
rights of those peacefully exercising their right to assemble without violence; thanked Congressman
Correa for talking with ICE administrators and for protecting the rights of those peacefully exercising
their right to assemble without violence; sentencing of former Supervisor Andrew Do and indictment of
Peter Pham; statement Andrew Do provided requesting leniency during his sentence blamed his actions
on the Board of Supervisors; Judge Selna will hold Andrew Do and his daughter jointly responsible for
restitution and hopes for full restitution of the money and costs incurred as a result of his corrupt actions;
requested County Counsel maintain a itemization of costs that have incurred with regard to the forensic
auditing of all contracts and expenses incurred by the County in order for the County to recover monies;
invited everyone to attend Flag Day ceremony on June 14th, 2pm at Baby Beach in Dana Point

Supervisor Wagner - Oral Re: Sentencing of former Supervisor Andrew Do shows the system works and
hopes full restitution is ordered; recognizes First Amendment right to protest without violence and hopes
law enforcement will exercise appropriate restraint; thanked Santa Ana Police Department, OC Sheriff
and County Executive Officer for keeping Board members informed

Chair Chaffee - Oral Re: Sentencing of former Supervisor Andrew Do and additional indictments
forthcoming; recognized the justified outrage of community members and supports their right to safely
protest peacefully with dignity; dedication and reopening of the Stanton and Brea Libraries and future
reopening of La Habra Library; thanked County departments that participated in the Future Leaders
Program held on Saturday, June 8

Bryan Kaye - Oral Re: County budget and lawsuit against District Attorney Spitzer resulting in $3 million

wife Judge Cheri Pham who presided over the courts; Supervisor Wagner's wife is a judge in probate
